item.title: Workrave 1.11.5
item.description:
Workrave 1.11.5 adds quiet micro-breaks, Windows power options during breaks, and GNOME Shell 51 support. It also improves tray menus and window visibility, and fixes problems with reading-mode timers, language selection, and sound preferences.
- New features and improvements: - Added a "Break in quiet-mode" option for micro-breaks, so their timer can keep running without automatic break reminders while rest-break reminders remain enabled (#743, Pedro Rolo) - Added support for GNOME Shell 51 - Added an option to hide the status window from the taskbar and window switcher on Windows and Linux/X11. This option is enabled by default (#701, #747) - Added shutdown, sleep, and hibernate options to the rest-break window on Windows (#735) - The Windows installer now supports `/NOLAUNCH` to skip starting Workrave after installation - Bug fixes: - Fixed reading-mode timers staying paused after leaving suspended mode (#724, #727, #739) - Fixed empty tray menus on Linux, including when using i3 with Polybar (#750) - Fixed the GNOME Shell menu not appearing after choosing "Open Workrave" (#750) - Fixed switches in the GNOME Shell menu not applying changes when dragged - Fixed Workrave ignoring the system language when no language was selected in preferences - Fixed crashes in Linux panel applets when Workrave's settings could not be found - The Linux indicator applet now respects the automatic-start setting - Fixed registry permission errors when installing Workrave for the current Windows user (#749) - Fixed blocking break windows appearing in the taskbar and window switcher on Windows and Linux/X11 (#747) - Fixed the preferences window opening when dismissing the Windows tray menu (#720) - The Windows tray menu now follows the selected light or dark appearance (#715) - Fixed the selected sound theme being shown incorrectly when reopening sound preferences (#702)

commit 66527be0a012add6d52524977433628eed1cd80f Author: winfij Date: 2026-09-02T23:54:44+02:00
Fix test_reading_mode_suspend for corrected suspend-resume insensitive mode
The rest-break restart after resume was previously never observed, because the insensitive-mode reset on resume depended on stop_all_breaks()'s conditional side effect (BreakControl::is_active()), which doesn't fire when no break is active at suspend time. With the explicit, unconditional set_insensitive_mode_all_breaks() reset, the rest break now correctly restarts, so the previously-disabled expectations are restored (with corrected timings, verified against a local test run: prelude at t=1680, break start delay of 9s, and an observed break duration of 308s rather than the originally sketched 300s).
(cherry picked from commit dde51c0b132325f84ad28987d0b31e624f3be94d)
